news.title: Africa’s 54 football associations could share $1.35 billion as FIFA prepares new funding offer after World Cup windfall
news.lede: The reported plan provides $25 million for each national association, within a broader $6.35 billion development fund. Africa has 54 member associations. Applying the proposed payment equally across those members produces a potential continental total of $1.35 billion, subject to approval and the final funding conditions. That figure is a calculation rather than an allocation announced for Africa.

news.title: Aussie stars, coach could be denied chance for final title
news.lede: A number of Socceroos stars may be robbed of their last chance to win silverware, with talks the Asian Cup could be postponed due to conflict in Saudi Arabia. FIFA announced on Thursday it had postponed the FIFAe Finals scheduled to take place in Jeddah this weekend due to the Houthi missile and drone attacks, with questions about whether the kingdom will host other planned events now rising. Popovic has not said if he will stay on after the Asian Cup. In less than three months until the Asian Cup kicks off in Saudi Arabia, all nations as well as the Asian Football Confederation are monitoring the attacks in the area.

news.title: “We Must Be Patient Against Defensive Teams” — Busari Reveals Flamingos’ World Cup Strategy Ahead of Morocco 2026
news.lede: Flamingos head coach Akeem Busari has identified patience, tactical discipline and improved decision-making in attack as key areas Nigeria must master ahead of the 2026 FIFA Under-17 Women’s World Cup in Morocco. With the tournament scheduled to begin on October 17, Busari revealed that the coaching crew has been working to improve the team’s ability to break down opponents who defend deep and restrict attacking space. “One of our basic philosophies is that we want to keep the ball on the ground, we want to play to the flank, we want to have our crosses and we finish our work,” Busari said. The coach explained that recent preparations have highlighted the difficulties of playing against teams that commit several players to defending.

news.title: “I’ve Won WAFCON, Played at the World Cup and Olympics, But I Want More” — Echegini Hungry for Greater Super Falcons Success
news.lede: Super Falcons midfielder Jennifer Echegini has declared that her ambition to achieve more with Nigeria remains stronger than ever, insisting that previous appearances at the World Cup and Olympics, alongside winning the Women’s Africa Cup of Nations, have only increased her desire for further success. The Paris Saint-Germain midfielder, speaking about her international career and Nigeria’s ambitions, explained that representing the Super Falcons carries a responsibility that goes beyond playing club football. “The Super Falcons have a lot of fans, a lot of pride, a lot of history with their country, so there’s a lot of weight to carry,” Echegini said. “I feel like there’s more responsibility than playing for a club would have.”

news.title: Flamingos settle in Rabat ahead of U-17 World Cup opener
news.lede: Coach Akeem Busari’s side completed their final training session in Casablanca on Monday evening before travelling to the Moroccan capital on Tuesday. The players subsequently participated in a light training session as preparations intensified for their opening Group B encounter. The Nigerian contingent is accommodated at the Complexe Sportif Feminin. The Flamingos will face Poland at the Mohammed VI Football Complex, Pitch 4, on Saturday, with kick-off scheduled for 8pm.

news.title: New Zealand select squad for first FIFA U-15 Boys World Cup in Azerbaijan
news.lede: New Zealand Football have named their squad for the inaugural FIFA U-15 World Cup & Festival, starting in Azerbaijan this month. The squad includes six players from Wellington Phoenix, three from Auckland United, two from Christchurch United and one each from Nomads United, Bay Olympic and Fencibles United. Unlike traditional FIFA age-group tournaments, the competition will use an eight-a-side format, with matches comprising two 20-minute halves. The team will be coached by Wellington Phoenix’s head of boys’ talent development and men’s U-18 head coach, Cam Grieve.
